the use of personal computers in organizations has a number of important implications for information systems and organizational design.
the use of personal computers in the office has a negative effect on the performance of clerical tasks.

the following factors have a significant effect on the use of information systems: 1. the user's level of education, 2. the user's attitude to computers, 3. the user's perception of usefulness of the system, 4. the user's self-confidence, 5. the user's perceived control over the system, 6. the user's experience of the system.

the design of a new generation of distributed systems that can be used to provide a new generation of applications for the end-user.
the integration of distributed PC workstations in the organization and operation of information processing in a company.
the integration of personal computers into an organisation's information processing system.

the integration of PC workstations into a company’s IT environment is a complex task that can be accomplished by using a well-structured approach.
the PC is a very important tool for the future, but not the ultimate one.

the integration of PC workstations in the organizational structure of the information processing of an organization has a considerable influence on the design of the organizational system, on the practical management of decentralized hardware and software resources, and on the design of a new organizational information system.

we have been successful in developing and implementing a PC workstation concept which has been integrated into the organizational structure and management of information processing.
the integration of distributed personal computers into the organization and operation of the information processing system is a major challenge to the management of information technology.
the PC workstation is a new and important tool for information processing in organizations.

the integration of PC workstations in the organization and operation of the information processing is not only a technical but also an organizational task.
